title: General Electric Co. v. EPA (2002)
summary: EPA’s PCB risk-assessment guidance imposed binding choices and therefore required legislative-rule procedures.

sections.Parties: General Electric petitioned for review of EPA’s PCB Risk Assessment Review Guidance Document. EPA administered disposal and cleanup rules under the Toxic Substances Control Act.
sections.Material Facts: The regulations allowed applicants to propose alternatives to standard PCB cleanup and disposal methods if they would not create unreasonable risk. The guidance required an applicant either to use a specified total-toxicity factor of 4.0 or to calculate cancer and specified noncancer risks separately. GE argued that the document bound applicants and the agency; EPA emphasized its guidance label, alternative methods, and allowance for unusual cases.
sections.Procedural History: GE sought direct review in the D.C. Circuit. The court examined the document’s language and the agency’s account of its application, then granted the petition and vacated the document for failure to use the procedures required by the APA and TSCA.
sections.Issue: Was the document an exempt policy statement or a legislative rule imposing binding obligations?
sections.Holding: The document was a legislative rule. Its commands and the agency’s implementation established binding effects, so issuing it without the required procedures was unlawful.
sections.Reasoning: The practical inquiry concerned whether EPA genuinely remained willing to entertain alternatives. Allowing two prescribed methods did not allow a third. The document required specified risks to be considered and represented that the default factor would be accepted. A clause allowing unusual components in unusual cases did not make its commands tentative in ordinary cases. EPA identified no application accepting an unprescribed method, omitting required risk categories, or rejecting use of the default factor. The court therefore found facial binding effect unrefuted by practice. The accompanying notes distinguish pressure to comply with a tentative policy from a present command and connect binding effect to APA finality; boilerplate disclaimers alone may be insufficient.
